title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages): k is a field of characteristic ≠ 2 and E is an elliptic curve with tangent line t_E at the origin. J is a 3-element index set, presumably the three non-trivial 2-torsion points, i.e. the three roots e_i of the Weierstrass cubic. V_J(k) = Ker(k^J → k, sum) is a 2-dimensional space. Σ_J is the associated P^1, with V_J(k) ≅ Γ(Σ_J, O(1)). The point t of Σ_J is attached to E. There is a canonical exact sequence 0 → F_t → V_J(k) → O_t(1) → 0, with F_t ≅ O_t(-1)(ω), where ω is the torsor of 'ω' choices. α: μ_4^×(k) ≅ ω is an auxiliary identification. On p.118 the iso k: t_E ≅ O_t(1) was pinned down by requiring that k^{⊗2} match a canonical iso t_E^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t}; this fixes k up to sign for fixed α, and up to μ_4 otherwise.

This page re-encodes k in coordinates, with the Legendre normal form as the goal. The chain of equivalences is:
(1) Giving k is the same as giving its dual ǩ: ť_E ≅ O_t(1)^∨ = O_t(-1) → O_t(-1)(ω) ≅ F_t. The middle arrow uses a chosen ω.
(2) That is the same as a monomorphism ť_E ↪ V_J(k) ⊂ k^J with image exactly F_t.
(3) That is the same as a nonzero element of V_J(t_E) = t_E ⊗ V_J(k) = Ker(t_E^J → t_E, sum).

So k amounts to a family (δ_i)_{i∈J} of vectors in t_E subject to three conditions:
(a) Σ δ_i = 0, i.e. the family lies in V_J(t_E).
(b) A proportionality condition: the line in V_J(k) cut out by the map ξ ↦ (⟨ξ, δ_i⟩)_i is F_t.
(c) The 'Legendre pinning' (épinglage de Legendre) condition: k^{⊗2} is the standard iso already known from (77).

He then chooses a nonzero δ ∈ t_E and ω ∈ ω, and writes δ_i = φ_i^ω(δ)·δ with scalars φ_i^ω(δ) ∈ k^*. Independence of the δ_i from the choice of δ gives the homogeneity φ_i^ω(λδ) = λ^{-1} φ_i^ω(δ).

The next page translates (a)–(c) into conditions on the φ_i:
- Σ_i φ_i = 0;
- the vector (φ_i) spans F_t;
- the pinning fixes the φ_i up to sign;
- the ω-dependence is given by an α(ω) factor.

The purpose is an intrinsic (choice-free) description of the Legendre form / level-2 structure of an elliptic curve. The φ_i play the role of weight-1 modular quantities: up to normalisation they look like square roots of differences of the e_i, which is where μ_4 and signs enter.
errors: Item (b) writes k: t_E ≅ F_t → O_t(1). Strictly, the family (δ_i) defines ť_E ≅ F_t, i.e. the dual ǩ, since F_t ≅ O_t(-1)(ω) and not O_t(1). This is a minor slip in notation, not in logic.
The equivalence of (3) with (2) silently requires the nonzero element to also satisfy (b). Grothendieck makes this explicit in the next lines, so there is no real gap.

ideas.what: Encoding a trivialisation of the tangent line t_E as a sum-zero family (δ_i)_{i∈J} in t_E indexed by the 2-torsion / Weierstrass roots, constrained by a proportionality condition and a Legendre pinning.
ideas.modern_name: Level-2 (Legendre) structure on elliptic curves; weight-1 modular forms for Γ(2), with t_E^{⊗-k} giving the weight-k line bundle (Katz-style intrinsic modular forms).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); the intrinsic formulation is due to Deligne, Katz (1973) and Igusa.

ideas.what: The coordinate functions φ_i^ω(δ), homogeneous of degree −1 in δ, together with a twisting by a μ_4-torsor ω.
ideas.modern_name: Weight-1 modular functions / theta-null type quantities for Γ(4)/Γ(2) with μ_4-twist.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping: a linear-algebraic re-encoding of a trivialisation of t_E in terms of sum-zero families indexed by the 2-torsion. It serves an intrinsic treatment of the Legendre form that is well covered by the Deligne/Katz/Igusa theory. There is no new result or connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'épi-glyphe [?] de Legendre' should read 'épinglage de Legendre' (Legendre pinning).
'(δ_i)_{i∈J} ∈ t_E^{⊗J}' should be '(δ_i)_{i∈J} ∈ t_E^J' (a family of vectors in t_E).
'V_J(t_E) = t_E ⊗ Ker(t_E^J → t_E)': the leading 't_E' (or 't_E ⊗') is struck out in the image. The intended formula is V_J(t_E) = Ker(t_E^J →(sum) t_E).
In (c), 'k^{⊗2}' is written with ⊗2 ('que k^{⊗2} est un isom. standard déjà connu').

The equation labels in the margin are (82) for the family, (83) for the bracket of conditions a–c, (84) for δ_i = φ_i^ω(δ)δ and (85) for the homogeneity relation. They are hard to read but consistent with the next page.
'δ ∈ t_E^*' means t_E minus {0}, i.e. a nonzero tangent vector, not the dual space.
